headline: TSLA surges +6.69% on July 6 — biggest Magnificent 7 gainer as market anticipates Lars Moravy's July 7 Giga Texas 'cool news' announcement on Cybercab production scaling; Dow crosses 53,000 for first time in history; AI-tied stocks lead broad rally (AMD +6.5%, QCOM +6%); Nasdaq-100 +1.43%, S&P 500 +0.87%; TSLA closed $419.77 (+$26.32) vs prior close of $393.45; stock now up ~6.7% YTD and +33% over past year (Investopedia / Yahoo Finance, Jul 6, 2026)

Electrek: Cybercab — 100+ units in Giga Texas outbound lot but unsupervised fleet shrinking to ~14 vehicles — Tesla is mass-producing a steering-wheel-less Cybercab it cannot yet sell or drive itself at scale; production-before-autonomy tension crystallized; Austin unsupervised fleet slid from peak ~25 active vehicles to ~14 as safety validation lags manufacturing; FSD crash rate ~4x human urban baseline per NHTSA; Musk confirmed robotaxi 'not material until 2027'; NHTSA self-cert path eliminates 2,500-unit cap so production scaling is uncapped; commercial passenger service gated by FSD v15 (end-2026/early 2027); manufacturing S-curve executing ahead of software timeline (Electrek, Jul 6, 2026)

Giga Texas July 6 aerial: 4 simultaneous production ramps confirmed — Cybercabs accumulating in outbound lot alongside Model Y L units and fresh Cybertrucks; drone journalist Joe Tegtmeyer captures 'everything building at once' just 24 hours ahead of VP Lars Moravy's promised July 7 announcement; Cybercab lot inventory confirms volume production pace building since April ramp; Model Y L units lined up less than a week after July 1 US launch; Tesla's most parallel production schedule ever — Cybercab + Cybertruck + Model Y L + Optimus factory construction all running simultaneously at a single site; community sources expect July 7 announcement to cover Cybercab production scaling milestone or commercial Cybercab launch confirmation for Houston (basenor / Joe Tegtmeyer on X, Jul 6, 2026)

Tesla Q2 2026 earnings July 22 preview — automotive gross margin the single most-watched metric after stock dropped ~7% on an 18% delivery beat; market questions whether 480K deliveries came with higher ASPs or incremental discounting; Q1 2026 auto gross margin was 21.1%; consensus expects Q2 margin pressure from Model Y L launch costs, Semi ramp, and Cybercab early production inefficiencies; bulls argue delivery leverage should improve margins while bears cite China price war; near-100% margin robotaxi economics could provide a Q2 upside surprise if Cybercab commercial revenue registers for first time; July 7 Giga Texas production milestone may set the pre-earnings narrative (TradingKey / MEXC / MarketBeat, Jul 6, 2026)

Morningstar raises TSLA fair value estimate to $450 (from $425) post Q2 delivery blowout — says robotaxi accounts for 35%, FSD subscriptions ~20%, and Optimus sales/subscriptions ~30% of fair value estimate; maintains 'narrow-moat' designation; separate analyst (Equal Weight, $415 PT) calls stock 'fully-priced' at current levels; TSLA trading $389–$438 intraday July 6 (+3.63%) as market recovers from post-Q2-report selloff and positions ahead of July 7 Giga Texas announcement; stock has surrendered ~6% YTD 2026, trading between $337–$458 in H1 (Morningstar / Yahoo Finance / TradingKey, Jul 6, 2026)

Tesla Miami Robotaxi goes LIVE for rider service — first driverless rides outside Texas completed July 5-6; Tesla officially announced 'service is now available in Miami' on X July 5; geofenced area covers West Miami, Doral, and Coral Gables including Miami International Airport (MIA); Model Y fleet operational with no driver or safety monitor; first public rider videos and walkaround footage circulating on social media; TechTimes notes Florida's tropical rain is the hardest test yet for camera-only FSD — operating in precipitation, high humidity, and complex multi-lane airport approach roads; confirms Miami is Tesla's first operational driverless city outside Texas (gurufocus / TipRanks / TechTimes, Jul 5–6, 2026)

Tesla caps employee AI tool spending at $200/week effective July 6 — Grok exempt; engineers had been burning thousands of tokens weekly before the policy; management approval required for overages; third-party AI products (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) subject to the cap while xAI's Grok remains uncapped — signals Tesla's preference for Musk's in-house AI as the enterprise standard and deepens xAI-Tesla operational integration; joins Uber, Meta, and Walmart in instituting token cost controls as enterprise AI bills soar (Electrek / The Information / TechTimes, Jul 3–6, 2026)

Tesla launches unsupervised Robotaxi service in Miami, Florida — first expansion outside Texas, making Miami the 4th city and Florida the 1st state beyond Texas to offer fully driverless rides; geofenced area covers West Miami, Doral, and Coral Gables (~10–14 sq mi) including Miami International Airport (MIA); Model Y fleet initially, with Cybercab expected to join as production scales later in 2026; Coral Gables fire crews completed Tesla emergency response training ahead of launch; service is phased app-based rollout at introductory flat rate + applicable fees; Florida law permits fully driverless vehicles meeting federal standards; Miami's tropical climate, airport traffic, and multilingual rider base mark a distinct operating environment from Austin/Bay Area; confirms Tesla's multi-city expansion is accelerating beyond Texas as originally targeted in 1H 2026 roadmap (@Tesla Robotaxi / basenor / notateslaapp, Jul 3, 2026)

Tesla bundles free 1-year FSD subscription + free Supercharging + free Premium Connectivity with Model Y L Launch Series ($61,990 US) — first time Tesla has packaged a full 12-month FSD trial into a new US vehicle launch; TSLA stock recovers to $418-$424 (+1-2%) on July 3 as market positions ahead of July 7 Giga Texas announcement and July 22 Q2 earnings call (officially confirmed by Tesla IR); Giga Texas July 7 announcement expected to cover Cybercab production scaling milestone per VP Lars Moravy's teaser (Benzinga / notateslaapp / basenor, Jul 3, 2026)

Tesla Q2 2026 BLOWOUT: 480,126 deliveries (+25% YoY, +34% QoQ) — smashes 406K consensus by 74K and beats even the most bullish Wall St estimates (Goldman/JPMorgan 420K, Barclays 418K); Tesla's best-ever Q2 and first YoY delivery growth since 2023; drew down inventory (delivered 28K more than produced — reversal of Q1's 50K inventory build); Model 3/Y: 467,762; Other: 12,364; energy: 13.5 GWh +40% YoY; BYD BEV gap narrows from 220K to 77K (BYD 557K BEV, -8% YoY; Tesla +25%); TSLA stock dropped — market awaits Jul 22 earnings to see if volume recovery translated to margin (Electrek / CNBC / Yahoo Finance, Jul 2, 2026)
